briefdescription.para: Return true if the specified terminator checks to see if a value is equal to constant integer value.
Given a value comparison instruction, decode all of the 'cases' that it represents and return the 'default' block.

If TI is known to be a terminator instruction and its block is known to only have a single predecessor block, check to see if that predecessor is also a value comparison with the same value, and if that comparison determines the outcome of this comparison.

detaileddescription.para: If so, simplify TI. This does a very limited form of jump threading.

briefdescription.para: The specified terminator is a value equality comparison instruction (either a switch or a branch on "X == c").

detaileddescription.para: See if any of the predecessors of the terminator block are value comparisons on the same value. If so, and if safe to do so, fold them together.

briefdescription.para: This is called when we find an icmp instruction (a seteq/setne with a constant) as the only instruction in a block that ends with an uncond branch.

detaileddescription.para: We are looking for a very specific pattern that occurs when "A == 1 || A == 2 || A == 3" gets simplified. In this case, we merge the first two "or's of icmp" into a switch, but then the default value goes to an uncond block with a seteq in it, we get something like:
switch i8 A, label DEFAULT [ i8 1, label end i8 2, label end ] DEFAULT: tmp = icmp eq i8 A, 92 br label end end: ... = phi i1 [ true, entry ], [ tmp, DEFAULT ], [ true, entry ]
We prefer to split the edge to 'end' so that there is a true/false entry to the PHI, merging the third icmp into the switch.

briefdescription.para: Hoist any common code in the successor blocks up into the block.

detaileddescription.para: This function guarantees that BB dominates all successors. If AllInstsEqOnly is given, only perform hoisting in case all successors blocks contain matching instructions only. In that case, all instructions can be hoisted and the original branch will be replaced and selects for PHIs are added.

briefdescription.para: Speculate a conditional basic block flattening the CFG.

detaileddescription.para: Note that this is a very risky transform currently. Speculating instructions like this is most often not desirable. Instead, there is an MI pass which can do it with full awareness of the resource constraints. However, some cases are "obvious" and we should do directly. An example of this is speculating a single, reasonably cheap instruction.

There is only one distinct advantage to flattening the CFG at the IR level: it makes very common but simplistic optimizations such as are common in instcombine and the DAG combiner more powerful by removing CFG edges and modeling their effects with easier to reason about SSA value graphs.
An illustration of this transform is turning this IR: BB: %cmp=icmpult%x,%y bri1%cmp,label%EndBB,label%ThenBB ThenBB: %sub=sub%x,%y brlabelBB2 EndBB: %phi=phi[%sub,%ThenBB],[0,%BB] ...

simplesect.para: true if the conditional block is removed.
